title: awa-hkstar-1998-heavyweight
label: Marvelous Mike

won.source: Won the title at the federation's own pay-per-view, Slaughter in the Hell, per the federation's own 5 December 1998 recap.

note: Followed a roughly four-month reign by Dream King, who dropped the title at this same event; no document survives naming when, where, or how Dream King's own reign began, so that prior reign is not structured as its own row here.

won.source: Billed as a three-month reign in the promotion's own 16 February 1999 Battle Royal result.

lost.source: Pinned by Bob Peil after a powerbomb.

won.source: Pinned Canadian Thunder with a powerbomb.

title: awa-hkstar-1998-light-heavyweight
label: "Attitude, Inc."

won.source: Billed as champion entering the promotion's own Battle Royal pay-per-view; no earlier document survives.

note: Retained by disqualification after Tammy Lynn Sytch's interference against the challenger, Steel.

won.source: Defeated Steve Walker in a brawl that ended with Walker choked unconscious in a restaurant's fishing pool.

title: awa-hkstar-1998-intercontinental
label: Steve Walker

won.source: Billed as champion throughout the promotion's own Battle Royal pay-per-view; no earlier document survives.

note: Not defended at this event; the champion instead lost the promotion's own Hardcore Championship on the same card.

title: awa-hkstar-1998-heavyweight
label: Dream King

won.source: Made Jack Morris submit in the promotion's own Battle Royal pay-per-view main event, called the World Championship in that document.

note: The document calls this title the World Championship; a later served document from the same wing (12 September 1999) ties the name to the same Heavyweight Championship lineage.
